findings.reason: The protected Python is clear, conventional, and expert-interview ready. graph and indegree expose topological state, prerequisite/course and next_course make edge direction explicit, queue names current availability, and completed/semesters track the two verdict quantities directly. Freezing range(len(queue)) makes the semester boundary visible without a sentinel or duplicated queues; no material improvement warrants a candidate.

Every initial zero-indegree course has no unmet prerequisite and is eligible in semester one. Each loop freezes the starting queue length, so it processes exactly the courses eligible before that semester and defers newly unlocked courses to the next. Every relationship is removed once when its prerequisite course completes, and a dependent enters the queue only when its last unmet prerequisite reaches zero. The layers therefore assign every course its earliest legal semester. If fewer than n courses are processed, the remaining subgraph has no zero-indegree vertex and contains a directed cycle, requiring -1.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 1136, Python/Python 3, and Solution.minimumSemesters. Authenticated source evidence confirms one-based course labels, unique directed prerequisite pairs, unlimited same-semester parallelism, completion of every prerequisite before its dependent course, the minimum-semester objective, and the -1 impossibility sentinel. It also confirms n and relation-count bounds through 5000, distinct endpoints, and two-value relation rows; solve(n, relations) preserves all of these semantics.

Building the graph and indegree array costs O(n + r). Each course enters and leaves the queue once, and every relation is traversed once when its prerequisite completes, so total time is O(n + r). The adjacency list, indegrees, and queue collectively use O(n + r) space, matching the branch manifest exactly.
